The counsel for Jdr.No.2 submitted that he has made a proposal for settlement, the RFA is pending before Hon'ble High Court filed by him challenging the preliminary decree and he prays time by adjourning the auction of property. The counsel for Dhr. Opposed the applications and submitted that Jdr.No.2 has not challenged the order on FDP, RFA is not pending, Jdr.No.2 has got opportunity to participate in the auction and to purchase the property and prayed for dismissal. The grounds stated in the applications that the Jdr.No.2 intend to secure the witness to the Will and made application before Hon'ble High Court for restoration of MFA Ex.No.108/2024 No.1723/2022. Accordingly, I.A.No.3 is rejected. [S. NATARAJ] VI ACC & SJ., B'LURU CITY Await for Commissioner report. Call on 31-08-2024. VI ACC & SJ., B'luru.

Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

Respondent and Advocate: DURGA PROJECTS AND INFRASTRUCTURE PVT LTD
Hearing Judge: CCH43 XLII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
Business Text: This EP is filed by DHR to enforce the order passed by KRERA in Complaint No.CMP/UR/220629/0000969 dated: 25.05.2023. In EP the amount sought is Rs.79,83,389/- and also possession of the schedule property and execution of the registered sale deed in favour of the DHR. JDR filed objection to main petition stating that Civil court has no jurisdiction to execute the order passed by the KRERA. The KRERA has not followed the due procedure while passing the impugned order. So, it prayed to dismiss the petition with cost. Heard both side on maintainability of the EP. Perused the materials on record. Counsel for DHR produced Order passed by KRERA dated: 24.08.2023 which discloses that the present DHR has filed application for transfer of the EP to City Civil Court and accordingly it was transferred to this court for execution. But, KRERA has not passed considered order stating that it is unable to execute the order. So, as per Rule 26 of KRERA the Authority itself has got jurisdiction to execute its order. But, in this case authority has not given any reasons for transfer of the order to Civil Court for execution of the same. The citation relied by the JDR in WP No.17821/2025 clubbed with WP 18348/2025 and WP 19184/2025 dated: 31.10.2025 Mantri Developer Pvt Ltd., Vs. Sunil Veetil is directly applicable to the facts of this case. In said case the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka by considering the judgment of Hon’ble Apex Court was pleased to hold that Civil Court has no jurisdiction to execute the order passed by the KRERA as the said order does not fall under the definition of decree-Sec.2(2) of the CPC. covered under the definition of decree. Therefore, the appropriate remedy available to the DHR is to approach KRERA itself and seek for execution of the order passed by it in Complaint No.CMP/UR/220629/0000969 dated: 25.05.2023. Accordingly, this EP is dismissed as not at all maintainable before Civil Court.

No.1 This I.A. is filed by the judgment-debtors under Section 33 and 34 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, seeking direction to the decree-holder, to pay stamp duty as per Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, on the Arbitral Award passed by the Deputy Registrar of Chits, Sahakara Sadana, Bangalore, in Dispute No.DRB/CFS/DIS. No.4/94/2022-23. In the event of non-compliance, the judgment-debtors prays for impounding of the said Award under Section 33 of the Karnataka Stamp Act. 2. The decree-holder has orally objected to the I.A., relying on the judgment of Hon’ble Karnataka High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013 (Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Ltd. vs. K.V. Chandrashekar & Anr.) (NC: 2024:KHC:42774), contending that, the Arbitral Award, being for recovery of money, does not attract stamp duty under the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, as it does not involve movable or immovable
Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex.No.175/2024 property. 3. The judgment-debtors contended that, Arbitral Award is an "instrument" under the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 and is chargeable with stamp duty under Article 11. It is alleged that the decree-holder failed to pay the requisite stamp duty and court fees while filing the execution petition, rendering the Award liable to be impounded under Section 33 and inadmissible under Section 34 of the Act. The judgment- debtors further contended that, Award was passed exparte without giving them an opportunity to be heard and the decree- holder defaulted on chit fund installments, making the claim dubious. 4. The decree-holder relies on the ruling of Hon’ble Karnataka High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013, which held that Arbitral Awards for monetary claims, such as damages or loan recovery, do not fall under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, as they do not involve tangible movable or immovable property. It is submitted that the present Award, being for recovery of money arising from chit fund dispute, is exempt from stamp duty as per the cited precedent. The decree-holder asserts that the judgment-debtors' procedural objections i.e., Exparte Award are irrelevant to the stamp duty issue and should be raised in a separate proceeding under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. 5. Arbitral Award in question pertains to recovery of money arising from Chit Fund Agreement, wherein the decree- 4 Ex.No.175/2024 holder subscribed to a chit. Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, prescribes stamp duty for Arbitral Awards involving immovable or movable property. However, the Hon’ble Karnataka High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013 has categorically held that Awards dealing with monetary claims, such as damages or loan recovery, do not qualify as movable property under Article 11, as the article applies only to tangible properties. Such Awards are not subject to stamp duty due to their intangible nature and legislative oversight in the Act. 6. The Hon’ble High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013 further clarified that courts cannot fill legislative gaps by imposing stamp duty on Awards for damages. This precedent is directly applicable to the present case, as the Award does not involve tangible movable or immovable property but pertains to monetary claim. 7. The reliance of judgment-debtors on Sections 33 and 34 of the Karnataka Stamp Act is misplaced, as the Award is not chargeable with stamp duty in the first place. Consequently, there is no basis for impounding the Award under Section 33 or declaring it inadmissible under Section 34. The objections of judgment-debtors regarding procedural irregularities in the arbitral process i.e., Exparte Award, lack of opportunity to be heard are beyond the scope of this I.A. Such objections pertain to the validity of the Award and must be raised in a separate challenge under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as held by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in M. Anasuya Devi vs. M. Manik Reddy; 2003 ( 8 ) SCC 565. 5 Ex.No.175/2024 8. The contention that the Chit Agreement is unregistered is irrelevant, as the Award itself is the instrument under consideration for execution, not the underlying Agreement. In light of the ruling of Hon’ble High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013, the Arbitral Award in Dispute No.DRB/CFS/DIS. No.4/94/2022- 23, being for recovery of money (damages), does not attract stamp duty under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. The decree-holder is not required to pay stamp duty and the Award is admissible in evidence for execution proceedings without additional stamping. The prayer to impound the Award under Section 33 or direct payment of stamp duty is unsustainable and liable to be rejected. Hence, this court proceed to pass the following:- ORDER I.A.No.1 filed by the judgment- debtors under Sections 33 and 34 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, is hereby dismissed. No order as to costs. No.4/94/2022-23. In the event of non-compliance, the judgment-debtors prays for impounding of the said Award under Section 33 of the Karnataka Stamp Act. 2. The decree-holder has orally objected to the I.A., relying on the judgment of Hon’ble Karnataka High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013 (Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Ltd. vs. K.V. Chandrashekar & Anr.) (NC: 2024:KHC:42774), contending that, the Arbitral Award, being for recovery of money, does not attract stamp duty under the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, as it does not involve movable or immovable
Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex.No.175/2024 property. 3. The judgment-debtors contended that, Arbitral Award is an "instrument" under the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 and is chargeable with stamp duty under Article 11. It is alleged that the decree-holder failed to pay the requisite stamp duty and court fees while filing the execution petition, rendering the Award liable to be impounded under Section 33 and inadmissible under Section 34 of the Act. The judgment- debtors further contended that, Award was passed exparte without giving them an opportunity to be heard and the decree- holder defaulted on chit fund installments, making the claim dubious. 4. The decree-holder relies on the ruling of Hon’ble Karnataka High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013, which held that Arbitral Awards for monetary claims, such as damages or loan recovery, do not fall under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, as they do not involve tangible movable or immovable property. It is submitted that the present Award, being for recovery of money arising from chit fund dispute, is exempt from stamp duty as per the cited precedent. The decree-holder asserts that the judgment-debtors' procedural objections i.e., Exparte Award are irrelevant to the stamp duty issue and should be raised in a separate proceeding under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. 5. Arbitral Award in question pertains to recovery of money arising from Chit Fund Agreement, wherein the decree- 4 Ex.No.175/2024 holder subscribed to a chit. Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, prescribes stamp duty for Arbitral Awards involving immovable or movable property. However, the Hon’ble Karnataka High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013 has categorically held that Awards dealing with monetary claims, such as damages or loan recovery, do not qualify as movable property under Article 11, as the article applies only to tangible properties. Such Awards are not subject to stamp duty due to their intangible nature and legislative oversight in the Act. 6. The Hon’ble High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013 further clarified that courts cannot fill legislative gaps by imposing stamp duty on Awards for damages. This precedent is directly applicable to the present case, as the Award does not involve tangible movable or immovable property but pertains to monetary claim. 7. The reliance of judgment-debtors on Sections 33 and 34 of the Karnataka Stamp Act is misplaced, as the Award is not chargeable with stamp duty in the first place. Consequently, there is no basis for impounding the Award under Section 33 or declaring it inadmissible under Section 34. The objections of judgment-debtors regarding procedural irregularities in the arbitral process i.e., Exparte Award, lack of opportunity to be heard are beyond the scope of this I.A. Such objections pertain to the validity of the Award and must be raised in a separate challenge under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as held by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in M. Anasuya Devi vs. M. Manik Reddy; 2003 ( 8 ) SCC 565. 5 Ex.No.175/2024 8. The contention that the Chit Agreement is unregistered is irrelevant, as the Award itself is the instrument under consideration for execution, not the underlying Agreement. In light of the ruling of Hon’ble High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013, the Arbitral Award in Dispute No.DRB/CFS/DIS. No.4/94/2022- 23, being for recovery of money (damages), does not attract stamp duty under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. The decree-holder is not required to pay stamp duty and the Award is admissible in evidence for execution proceedings without additional stamping. The prayer to impound the Award under Section 33 or direct payment of stamp duty is unsustainable and liable to be rejected. Hence, this court proceed to pass the following:- ORDER I.A.No.1 filed by the judgment- debtors under Sections 33 and 34 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, is hereby dismissed. No order as to costs. (NC: 2024:KHC:42774), contending that, the Arbitral Award, being for recovery of money, does not attract stamp duty under the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, as it does not involve movable or immovable
Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex.No.175/2024 property. 3. It is alleged that the decree-holder failed to pay the requisite stamp duty and court fees while filing the execution petition, rendering the Award liable to be impounded under Section 33 and inadmissible under Section 34 of the Act. The judgment- debtors further contended that, Award was passed exparte without giving them an opportunity to be heard and the decree- holder defaulted on chit fund installments, making the claim dubious. 4. Arbitral Award in question pertains to recovery of money arising from Chit Fund Agreement, wherein the decree- 4 Ex.No.175/2024 holder subscribed to a chit. Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, prescribes stamp duty for Arbitral Awards involving immovable or movable property. Such Awards are not subject to stamp duty due to their intangible nature and legislative oversight in the Act. 6. The Hon’ble High Court in W.P.No.29299/2013 further clarified that courts cannot fill legislative gaps by imposing stamp duty on Awards for damages. Such objections pertain to the validity of the Award and must be raised in a separate challenge under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as held by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in M. Anasuya Devi vs. M. Manik Reddy; 2003 ( 8 ) SCC 565. 5 Ex.No.175/2024 8. No.4/94/2022- 23, being for recovery of money (damages), does not attract stamp duty under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. The decree-holder is not required to pay stamp duty and the Award is admissible in evidence for execution proceedings without additional stamping. Order Procedural History: 1 Ex.179/2024 PW-1 ದಿಃ14.02.2025 ರಂದುಸಾಕ್ಷಿಗೆಪ್ರಮಾಣವಚನಬೋ ಧಿಸಿದೆ. ಮುಂ ದುವರಿದಮುಖ್ಯವಿಚಾರಣೆ ಡಿಕ್ರಿದಾರರ ಪರಶ್ರೀ ಮತಿಹೆಚ್ . ಕೆ . ವಕೀಲರಿಂದಃ - ನಾನು ಈದಿವಸ ನನ್ನಮುಖ್ಯವಿಚಾರಣೆ ಶಪಥ ಪ್ರಮಾಣಪತ್ರಹಾಜರು ಪಡಿಸಿದ್ದು ಅದರಲ್ಲಿರುವಅಂಶಗಳುಸತ್ಯವಾಗಿದ್ದುಅದ ಕ್ಕೆನಾನುಸಹಿಮಾಡಿರುತ್ತೇನೆ. ಓ.ಎಸ್.6570/2015 ರತೀರ್ಪು ಮತ್ತು ಡಿಕ್ರಿಯದೃಢೀಕೃತನಕಲುಗಳನ್ನು ನಿಪಿ.1 ಮತ್ತು 2, ಕೆಂ ಪೇಗೌಡನಗರಪೊಲೀಸ್‍ಠಾಣೆಯವರು ನೀಡಿರುವಹಿಂಬರಹ ಮತ್ತು ದೂ ರಿನದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿ ನಿಪಿ.3, ಕೆಂ ಪೇಗೌಡನಗರಪೊಲೀಸ್‍ ಠಾಣೆಯವರು ನೀಡಿರುವಹಿಂಬರಹಮತ್ತು ದೂ ರಿನದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿನಿಪಿ.4, ಕೆಂ ಪೇಗೌಡನಗರಪೊಲೀಸ್‍ಠಾಣೆಗೆನೀಡಿರುವದೂ ರಿನಪ್ರತಿಮತ್ತು ಹಿಂಬರಹವನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿನಿಪಿ.5, ಕೆಂ ಪೇಗೌಡನಗರಪೊಲೀಸ್‍ ಠಾಣೆಗೆಅವರು ನೀಡಿರುವಸ್ವೀಕೃತಿ ಮತ್ತು ದುಾ ರಿನಪ್ರತಿಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿನಿಪಿ.6 , ಅಪರಾಧಸಂಖ್ಯೆ145/2024, ಎಫ್.ಐ.ಆರ್‍ ಮತ್ತುದೂ ರಿನದೃಢೀಕೃತನಕಲುಗಳನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟಾಗಿನಿಪಿ.7, ಪೊಲೀಸ್‍ರವರುನೀಡಿರುವ ಸ್ವೀಕೃತಿಯದೃಢೀಕೃತನಕಲನ್ನು ನಿಪಿ.8, ಒಟ್ಟು 12 ಫೋಟೋ ಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಸಿಡಿ ಹಾಜರುಮಾಡಿದ್ದುಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ನಿಪಿ.9 ರಿಂದ21 ಎಂದುಗುರುತಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ತೀರ್ಪು ಋಣಿದಾರರು ಏಕಪಕ್ಷೀಯವಾಗಿದ್ದು ಪಾಟೀ ಸವಾಲು ಇಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ಪರಿಗಣಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ( ತೆರೆದನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯದಲ್ಲಿನನ್ನಉಕ್ತಲೇಖನದರೀತ್ಯಾಬೆರಳಚ್ಚು ಮಾಡಲಾಯಿತು.) ಓ.ಹೇ.ಕೇ.ಸ.ಇ.ಎ.ಒ. (ಕೆ. ಶ್ರೀವಿದ್ಯಾ) 42 ನೇಅಪರನಗರಸಿವಿಲ್‍ ಮತ್ತು ಸತ್ರನ್ಯಾಯಾಧೀಶರು, ಬೆಂಗಳೂ ರು. OS.8403/2017 PW-1

Hearing Judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
Business Text: Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on the limitation. In this case the DHR has got the decree for recovery of money on 21.06.2011. The 12 yrs limitations to file the executing the decree will expires on 21.06.2023. But this petition being filed before this court on 05.02.2024, which is after lapse of more than 7 months 15 days. But L/c for the DHR submits that, the Hon\''ble Apex court in its sue moto WP(C) no.3/20 and Misc application no.21/22 , vide its order dt 10.01.2022 excluded the period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022 for the purpose of limitation. Thus he contended that, the said period is requires to be added to the remaining period commences from 01.03.2022 to file the petition. According to him as on 01.03.2022 the DHR has 1 yr 3 months 20 days time to file the petition, for which the saved period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022, which comes of 1 yr 11 months, 13 days are added to the 1 yr ,3 months 20 days, the total period available to the DHR to file petition is 3 yrs 3 months 3 days from 01.03.2022, said period will expires on 03.07.2025. As the petition is filed on 05.02.2024 itself the said petition is well in time. The contention of the DHR is cannot be accepted for the simple reason that, the Hon\''ble Apex court by considering the gravity of the Covid break down in the country was pleased to exclude the period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022 in the event if the limitation expires btw that period or limitation commences, in any of the circumstances the Hon\''ble Apex court hold that, 90 days period is available from 01.03.2022. If the remaining period of limitation is exceeding the 90 days in that event the longer period is going to be applied. If the said aspect are considered, the case of the DHR will not fall in any of the conditions. In fact the limitation to file the present petition was not expired btw the period excluded for the purpose of limitation by the Hon\''ble Apex court. In fact the DHR was having 1 yr, 3 months 20 days period from 01.03.2022 to file their petition, which expires on 03.07.2023 in that event the DHR should have been filed the present petition on or before 03.07.2023, but its been filed on 05.02.2024, as the present petition is filed after expiry of limitation period, thus petition do not survives for the execution. Thus petition is dismissed, as the decree is time barred

The brief facts of the petition is as follows:- The decree-holder filed the Original Suit in seeking declaration of ownership in respect of Schedule-A Property and consequential reliefs including eviction from Schedule-C Property and permanent injunction against interference. 2(a). The matter was settled through Lok Adalat wherein both parties filed a Compromise Petition under Order XXIII Rule 3 CPC, which was duly accepted by the Court and a decree was passed in terms of the compromise. As per the compromise: - Defendant agreed that possession of Schedule-C Property has already been handed over to the plaintiff (decree-holder). - Defendant acknowledged plaintiff’s absolute ownership over Schedule-A Property. - Both parties agreed to the creation of 2.5 x 6 ft. passage on eastern side of Schedule-C for mutual use. 3. The grounds urged in the Execution Petition is as
Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex. No.302/2024 follows: Despite the compromise and declaration of rights, the decree-holder alleges non-compliance and seeks directions for: - Delivery of possession of Schedule-C property; - Punishment under Rule 32(5) for violation of injunction; - Arrest and civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtor & - Enforcement of ownership declaration over Schedule-A. 4. The judgment-debtor has objected to the execution petition on the following grounds: - The Schedule-C property was already vacated and possession handed over prior to filing the compromise petition. - There is no violation of any court order or injunction decree. - The Execution Petition is premature and not maintainable. - In case of any factual ambiguity, the Court Commissioner may be appointed to ascertain physical possession. 5. Heard both sides. 6. Now, the points that would arise for my consideration are :- 1. Whether the decree-holder has established willful disobedience or 4 Ex. No.302/2024 non-compliance of the compromise decree dated 26.07.2023 passed in , so as to warrant execution under Order 21 Rule 32(5) CPC? 2. What order? 7. My findings on the above points are as under:- : In the negative. : As per final order below for the following; 8. : - Upon perusal of the compromise decree, it is evident that:- - The possession of Schedule-C property was already delivered to the decree-holder. - There is no specific act of disobedience alleged, except vague averments. - There is no substantial material or evidence such as site inspection report, etc., proving that the judgment- debtor is in wrongful possession post-decree. - Execution under Rule 32(5) is maintainable only upon clear proof of willful disobedience of a mandatory decree, which is lacking in the present case. 9. This court is of the opinion that prima facie compliance of the decree has already been recorded in the Lok Adalat proceedings and no separate delivery or contempt arises 5 Ex. No.302/2024 unless specific breach is proved. Accordingly, is answered in the negative. 10. :- In view of the above discussions, this court proceed to pass the following:- ORDER This execution petition is dismissed as not maintainable at this stage in the absence of material proof of non-compliance. Liberty is reserved to the decree- holder to file fresh proceedings if any subsequent violation or obstruction is committed by the judgment-debtor. No order as to costs. The grounds urged in the Execution Petition is as
Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex. No.302/2024 follows: Despite the compromise and declaration of rights, the decree-holder alleges non-compliance and seeks directions for: - Delivery of possession of Schedule-C property; - Punishment under Rule 32(5) for violation of injunction; - Arrest and civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtor & - Enforcement of ownership declaration over Schedule-A. 4. The judgment-debtor has objected to the execution petition on the following grounds: - The Schedule-C property was already vacated and possession handed over prior to filing the compromise petition. - There is no violation of any court order or injunction decree. - The Execution Petition is premature and not maintainable. - In case of any factual ambiguity, the Court Commissioner may be appointed to ascertain physical possession. 5. Heard both sides. 6. Now, the points that would arise for my consideration are :- 1. Whether the decree-holder has established willful disobedience or 4 Ex. No.302/2024 non-compliance of the compromise decree dated 26.07.2023 passed in , so as to warrant execution under Order 21 Rule 32(5) CPC? 2. What order? 7. This court is of the opinion that prima facie compliance of the decree has already been recorded in the Lok Adalat proceedings and no separate delivery or contempt arises 5 Ex. No.302/2024 unless specific breach is proved. Accordingly, is answered in the negative. 10. :- In view of the above discussions, this court proceed to pass the following:- ORDER This execution petition is dismissed as not maintainable at this stage in the absence of material proof of non-compliance. Liberty is reserved to the decree- holder to file fresh proceedings if any subsequent violation or obstruction is committed by the judgment-debtor. No order as to costs. The DHr had produced xerox copy of RFA No.285/2024 (EJE) wherein, it shows that the present JDr had challenged the decree passed by this Court and the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka by order dated 6.6.2024 has dismissed the appeal. 11. The application is accompanied by affidavit. Objection is filed by the decree holder. 2. In the affidavit accompanying the application the JDr states that, the plaintiff has Ex.No.318/2024 falsely sworn to an affidavit that he is the absolute owner of suit schedule property and authenticated genuine documents with reference to suit schedule property are not produced. Further submits, the ejectment suit is based on the title deeds. Only two documents with entire different description other than suit schedule property is submitted to the Trial Court. The documents produced are not related to the suit schedule property. The Hon’ble Court has not noticed the same and passing of the decree is erroneous. 3. Further submits, the plaintiff has issued a rent agreement of non-existing property and fraudulently collected rental for many years and made false submissions to the Hon’ble Court. The schedule described is incorrect. The name of the defendant is wrongly described as Mr.Ramesh Naik and not Mr.Mallari Ramesh Naik. Further states, there are many errors, illegalities and mistakes in the judgment and decree passed by the Court which is not legally enforceable. Hence, prays to permit the JDr to allow cross-examination as
Order Judicial Findings: Ex.No.318/2024 directed by Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No.21603/2023 and to say the delivery warrant till the needful corrections are made. 4. JDr has also not paid the costs which were imposed during the proceedings in . Further states, the intention of the JDr is to deprive the DHr from enjoying the fruits of the decree. Hence, prays for rejecting the application with cost. 5. The following points arise for my determination : 1) Whether there should be stay of delivery warrant and other Ex.No.318/2024 proceedings as sought in the application ? 2) What order ? 6. Heard the counsels. 7. My findings to the above points are as hereunder : : In the negative. : As per the final order for the following : 8. : - The counsel for JDr argued that the plaintiff has created the documents and obtained decree in his favour and reiterated the grounds described in the affidavit accompanying the application. Per contra, the counsel for the DHr argued that the JDr has challenged the decree before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA No.285/2024 (EJE) which has been dismissed. Hence, submitted to reject the application. 9. Heard the counsels and perused the record. The present execution petition is filed to Ex.No.318/2024 eject the JDr from the schedule property. As per the Judgment and Decree of this Court in dated 4.11.2023, the suit was decreed in favour of the plaintiff and the defendant/ JDr was directed to surrender the vacant possession of the suit schedule residential premises in favour of the plaintiff within three months from the date of decree and the defendant was directed to pay damages of Rs.19,000/- per month from the date of suit till recovery of vacant possession of the suit schedule premises. 10. The DHr had produced xerox copy of RFA No.285/2024 (EJE) wherein, it shows that the present JDr had challenged the decree passed by this Court and the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka by order dated 6.6.2024 has dismissed the appeal. 11. It is well settled principle that, the Executing Court has limited jurisdiction and cannot go beyond the decree.
Order Annexed Proceedings: Ex.No.318/2024 12. Since, the appeal filed by JDr before Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA No.285/2024 (EJE) is dismissed by order dated 6.6.2024, the JDr has no right to file present application seeking to stay delivery warrant and other reliefs as sought in the application. With this observation, I answer in the negative. 13. : - Based on the finding on , I proceed to pass the following : O R D E R I.A.No.1 filed by the JDr under Section 151 of C.P.C. is hereby dismissed with cost of Rs.3,000/-. As per the Judgment and Decree of this Court in dated 4.11.2023, the suit was decreed in favour of the plaintiff and the defendant/ JDr was directed to surrender the vacant possession of the suit schedule residential premises in favour of the plaintiff within three months from the date of decree and the defendant was directed to pay damages of Rs.19,000/- per month from the date of suit till recovery of vacant possession of the suit schedule premises. 10. The DHr had produced xerox copy of RFA No.285/2024 (EJE) wherein, it shows that the present JDr had challenged the decree passed by this Court and the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka by order dated 6.6.2024 has dismissed the appeal. 11. It is well settled principle that, the Executing Court has limited jurisdiction and cannot go beyond the decree.
Order Procedural History: Ex.No.318/2024 ORDER ON I.A.NO.1 I.A.No.1 is filed by the judgment debtor under Section 151 of C.P.C. for stay of delivery warrant and to stay further proceedings. The application is accompanied by affidavit. Objection is filed by the decree holder. 2. In the affidavit accompanying the application the JDr states that, the plaintiff has Ex.No.318/2024 falsely sworn to an affidavit that he is the absolute owner of suit schedule property and authenticated genuine documents with reference to suit schedule property are not produced. Further submits, the ejectment suit is based on the title deeds. Only two documents with entire different description other than suit schedule property is submitted to the Trial Court. The documents produced are not related to the suit schedule property. The Hon’ble Court has not noticed the same and passing of the decree is erroneous. 3. Further submits, the plaintiff has issued a rent agreement of non-existing property and fraudulently collected rental for many years and made false submissions to the Hon’ble Court. The schedule described is incorrect. The name of the defendant is wrongly described as Mr.Ramesh Naik and not Mr.Mallari Ramesh Naik. Further states, there are many errors, illegalities and mistakes in the judgment and decree passed by the Court which is not legally enforceable. Hence, prays to permit the JDr to allow cross-examination as
Order Judicial Findings: Ex.No.318/2024 directed by Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No.21603/2023 and to say the delivery warrant till the needful corrections are made. 4. JDr has also not paid the costs which were imposed during the proceedings in . Further states, the intention of the JDr is to deprive the DHr from enjoying the fruits of the decree. Hence, prays for rejecting the application with cost. 5. The following points arise for my determination : 1) Whether there should be stay of delivery warrant and other Ex.No.318/2024 proceedings as sought in the application ? 2) What order ? 6. Heard the counsels. 7. My findings to the above points are as hereunder : : In the negative. : As per the final order for the following : 8. : - The counsel for JDr argued that the plaintiff has created the documents and obtained decree in his favour and reiterated the grounds described in the affidavit accompanying the application. Per contra, the counsel for the DHr argued that the JDr has challenged the decree before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA No.285/2024 (EJE) which has been dismissed. Hence, submitted to reject the application. 9. Heard the counsels and perused the record. The present execution petition is filed to Ex.No.318/2024 eject the JDr from the schedule property. Business Text: Case called. Counsel for DHR present and files memo with details of jurisdictional police. ORDER ON IA DATED 03-08-2024. This I.A. is filed by the DHR U/S 151 of CPC seeking assisstance of jurisdictional police to the Bailiff to break open the lock for attaching movable properties of JDR. In accompanying affidavit to the I.A. it is stated by DHR that the JDR and his nieghbours and his family members did not allow them to their house by not opening the door for attaching movables of JDR intentionally and further they are making threats and creating fear and obstruct for execution of attachment of immovable property. On perusal of counter copy of previous warrant of attachment of movables the bailiff requested for police aid as the father of JDR obstructed him. The learned Counsel for DHR files a memo with details of jurisdictional police as the Thilak nagar Police Station. If this application is allowed will not cause hardship to other side as the police shall aid to break open with peacefull manner without disturbing anybody in the location of JDR. Hence, this Court proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A. filed by the DHR U/S 151 of CPC for assisstance of jurisdictional police is hereby allowed. Consequently, the concerned police officer of Thilak nagar Police Station is hereby directed to give aid to the bailiff to break open the lock for attaching movable properties of JDR in the address mentioned in this petition in peacefull manner without disturbing the public. Re-issue attachment warrant of movables with police help.

Order Procedural History: Ex.No.461/2024 09.04.2025 Present petition is filed by Decree Holder praying to direct Registrar, City Civil Court, Bengaluru to cancel the Sale Deed dated 25.10.2002, registered on 12.05.2005 made in favour of Judgment Debtor and restore it in favour of Decree Holder by means of registered Re-conveyance deed in respect of plaint schedule premises. In the accompanying affidavit it is sworn to by Decree Holder that the Judgment Debtor has entered appearance and matter is amicably settled and Compromise Petition under O.XXIII R.3 of C.P.C. was preferred by both parties and compromise petition was filed on 09.08.2023. After going through the terms of Compromise Petition it was allowed by City Civil Court, and it was decreed on 10.11.2023. Pursuant to the Compromise Petition, this petition is filed to get the schedule premises registered back in favour of Decree Holder. Judgment Debtor has appeared before the Court through his counsel and submitted no objection for executing Sale Deed through Court as per order in Misc.No.496/2023. Heard both counsel. On the basis of the petition averments and materials on record following points arise for consideration: 1. Whether the prayer sought in petition deserves to be allowed? 2. If so what order? Heard both learned counsel. Perused records. For the reasons assigned below, I answer aforesaid points as under: :: In the affirmative . :: As per final order for the following: :: To substantiate the contentions taken in this petition, petitioner has placed reliance of the joint Compromise Petition filed in Misc.Petition No.496/2023, order on Compromise Petition and decree in Misc.No.496/2023. Upon perusal of the orders passed in Misc.496/2023 on Compromise Petition this Court by its order dated 10.11.2023 has allowed the Compromise Petition filed by both parties under O.XXIII R.3 of C.P.C. R/W S.144 and 151 of C.P.C. and directed the office to draw compromise decree as per the terms mentioned in the compromise petition. In the said order it is observed that present Respondent had filed before III Addl. City Civil Court, Bengaluru for specific performance of Contract against one Bettappa. Said Bettappa and his sons filed R.F.A.No.344/1992 against the Judgment and Decree dated 16.04.1999 and later S.L.P.10879/2000 before Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, which was also disposed on 31.07.2000. Bettappa and his sons failed to execute Sale Deed and this Judgment Debtor had filed execution petition No.879/2000 and got Sale Deed
Order Judicial Findings: been legally given effect to in the said miscellaneous petition No.496/2023 and also no objection stated by the Judgment Debtor in this petition, having regard to facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record, present petition deserves to be allowed. Business Text: Case called out. DHR counsel present. I heard the arguments on I.A No.2 on the side of counsel for DHR. I.A No.2 filed U/o 26 Rule 10(c) of CPC praying to appoint the Sheristedar/ Court official as court Commissioner to present the documents and to execute Sale Deed for Registration in terms of the Decree. In the affidavit filed in support of I.A No.2, the DHR sworn that this Execution petition filed against JDR for execution of Decree but, the JDR has failed to execute Registered Sale Deed in favour of DHR in respect of schedule property. Hence, it is necessary to appoint Sheristedar/ Court official as court Commissioner to execute and Register Sale deed on behalf of this court. It is sworn that the DHR is ready to pay the Commissioner fee. The learned counsel for DHR submitted that DHR already deposited balance amount of Rs.45,00,000/- before this court on 27.02.2025 by way of D.D. I heard on side of learned counsel for DHR and perused the entire records. On perusal of records, it would go to show that since cause notice not served to JDR. Notice was served by way of substituted service of paper publication in Samyuktha Karnataka daily news paper dt:23.07.2025 which is held sufficient, but JDR not appeared before the court. This court passed Judgment and Decree in O.S No.3485/2018 and directed the defendant to execute Registered Sale Deed with respect to the plaint schedule property in favour of the plaintiff in terms of the Sale Agreement dt: 22.05.2015 by receiving balance Sale consideration amount within two months from the date of the Judgment and also directed to handover the possession of the plaint schedule property to the plaintiff by executing the Sale Deed. It is ordered that in case the defendant fails to execute the Sale deed the plaintiff is entitled to get the Sale Deed through the process of the court by depositing balance Sale consideration amount in the court. The JDR failed to execute the Registered Sale Deed in favour of DHR by receiving balance consideration amount. DHR already deposited balance consideration amount of Rs.45,00,000/- before this court. The Jdr is liberty to withdraw that Sale consideration amount. Hence, there is sufficient grounds made out by the DHR to appoint Sheristedar/ Court official as court Commissioner to present the documents and to execute Sale Deed for Registration in terms of the Decree. Hence, I.A No.2 filed U/o 26 Rule 10(c) of CPC is hereby Allowed. It is requested to Registrar, City Civil Court, Bengaluru to name and depute any of the Sheristedar/ Court official as court Commissioner. DHR counsel prays to furnish draft Sale Deed. Call for Draft Sale Deed by 26.09.2025.

Thus the petition is filed after expiry of limitation period, which deserves to be dismissed.

Case Title: TULASIRAM C vs GIRISH KUMAR S
Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
Court Room & Judge: 17-CCH12 XVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
Hearing Judge: CCH12 XVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
Business Text: The counsel for DHR filed a memo on 29.06.2024 stating that this execution is filed within 2 years. In original suit it was decreed exparte. Hence, notice is not necessary to the decree holder as this execution petition is filed within 2 years. Hence, prayed to dispense with the notice. This court presume on the above memo that, the DHR wrongly mentioned as notice to decree holder. But it is for notice to judgment debtor. In support of his memo, he has filed judgment in Vasanth Rao Vs. Raj Reddy dt. 02.12.2002 in AIR 2003 (NOC) 600 (AP) and submitted that in this citation the Hon\''ble High Court of AP dispense the issuance of notice to JDR. But, on perusal of the same citation it’s para no.7, it is opined by Hon’ble Justice that, “It does not mean that notice to the respondent is totally prohibited in all cases where the execution petition is filed within 2 years. I am of the view that even in such cases it is always open for the executing court, in exercise of it’s discretion to issue notice to meet the ends of justice. Where such discretion is judiciously exercise and particularly where reasons are recorded, it cannot be said that there is any error in the exercise of jurisdiction vested under law”. And finally the Hon\''ble High Court dismissed the said Civil Revision Petition. Now this court gone through the judgment and decree in O.S. No. 3218/2019 which is the executable decree under this petition. It is true that, that case is disposed on 27.02.2023 and this execution petition filed on 16.03.2024 which is within 2 years from the passing of that decree. But, in operative portion of the said judgment, it is clearly ordered as, “The defendant is hereby directed to execute the absolute sale deed in favour of Plaintiff in pursuance of the sale agreement dt. 20.07.2016 by receiving the balance sale consideration amount of Rs. 25 Lakh and hand over possession of the suit schedule property in favour of the Plaintiff. “In the event of defendant’s failure to execute and register the sale deed in favour of Plaintiff, the Plaintiff is at liberty to get sale deed through process of law”. Next to that, on perusal of the execution petition the first prayer is “direct the defendant to execute the absolute sale deed in favour of the decree holder”. Hence, it is clear that as the direction sought against the JDR to execute the sale deed and the execution of sale deed through court of law is subsequent one then it is necessary to issue notice to the defendant / JDR to execute the sale deed as per judgment and decree. Therefore, as per facts and circumstances of the case and above discussion this court is of the considered opinion that, the issuance of cause notice to JDR is very necessary. Hence, proceed to pass the following; ORDER The memo dt. 29.06.2024 filed by the DHR is hereby rejected. Issue cause notice to JDR through court and RPAD and the counsel for JDR directed to pay PF in the office. Call on 31.08.2024.

Thereby Execution petition is closed as fully satisfied. (MOHAMMED MOINUDDIN) XVI Addl.City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru

In the said decision, the decree-holder entered into loan agreement in Karnataka for the purchase of a car i.e., movable property. A dispute arose, leading to arbitration in Mumbai, where an Arbitral Award was issued on 08.06.2011 for ₹1,19,678/- plus interest and costs, totaling ₹2,07,870/-. The Award was sought to be enforced in Karnataka through execution proceedings in Ex.No.2830/2011 before the XIX Additional City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City. The Executing Court, on 24.04.2013, upheld office objection requiring the decree-holder to pay stamp duty of ₹7,181/- under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. 2. The decree-holder argued that the Arbitral Award, being akin to a court decree under Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, should not be subject to stamp duty in Karnataka. The Award was executed in Mumbai and stamped as per the Bombay Stamp Act, 1958 (with ₹100 non-judicial stamp). The decree-holder relied on judicial Ex. No.638/2024 precedents, including Sundaram Finance Ltd. v. Abdul Samad ; [(2018) 3 SCC 622] and Maharashtra Apex Corporation Ltd. v. Balaji G.; [2011 SCC OnLine Ker 4039], to argue that the award transcends territorial barriers and does not require additional stamp duty in Karnataka. 3. Section 3 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 charges instruments executed in Karnataka with stamp duty and instruments executed outside Karnataka but brought for use in the state are subject to duty as per the Act. Section 19: Requires payment of additional stamp duty for instruments executed outside Karnataka but brought for use within the state, to match the duty payable under the Karnataka Stamp Act. Article 11: Specifies stamp duty for arbitral awards: For immovable property, the duty is as per a conveyance under Article 20(1). For movable property, the duty is based on the amount or market value ( i.e. 3/4% for amounts up to ₹50 lakhs). Awards not involving movable or immovable property (i.e., monetary claims like damages or loan recovery) are not explicitly covered. Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996: Treats an arbitral award as a decree of the
Order Judicial Findings: Ex. No.638/2024 court for enforcement purposes, executable under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, without requiring the court to pass a formal decree. 4. The Hon’ble Karnataka High Court, in its judgment dated 23.10.2024, ruled in favour of the decree holder, setting aside the Executing Court’s order requiring payment of stamp duty. Key points from the judgment: The arbitral award was for the recovery of loan amount (₹1,19,678/- plus interest), related to a car i.e. movable property. However, the court held that an Arbitral Award granting recovery of loans does not qualify as an instrument chargeable under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, as it does not deal with tangible movable property. The Hon’ble High Court noted that the Executing Court erroneously applied stamp duty as if the Award pertained to immovable property. Even if treated as movable property, the Award for loan recovery does not fall under Article 11, as it involves intangible monetary claims rather than tangible property. The Hon’ble High Court emphasized that courts cannot fill legislative gaps by imposing stamp duty on awards not explicitly covered by the Act. 5. Hence, the office objection requiring payment of stamp duty was based on Article 11 of the Ex. No.638/2024 Karnataka Stamp Act. However, the Hon’ble High Court’s ruling clarifies that this provision does not apply to Arbitral Awards for monetary claims i.e., loan recovery. 6. The objection cannot be sustained because: - The Karnataka Stamp Act does not explicitly mandate stamp duty for awards dealing with liquidated damages or loan recovery. In the decision of Sundaram Finance Ltd. v. Abdul Samad; [(2018) 3 SCC 622]: Held that an Arbitral Award can be enforced anywhere in India without being tied to the jurisdiction where it was passed, and it is treated as a decree for execution purposes. 7. In Maharashtra Apex Corporation Ltd. v. Balaji G.; [2011 SCC OnLine Ker 4039]: Hon’ble Supreme Court Ruled that an Award executed outside Kerala and brought for enforcement does not require additional stamp duty under the Kerala Stamp Act, as it is executable as a decree. 8. Hence, in view of the above decisions, the decree-holder is not required to pay the deficit stamp duty as the Arbitral Award for loan recovery does not attract stamp duty under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. Hence, proceed to pass the following: Ex. No.638/2024 ORDER Office objection raised by the office is not sustainable. XI Addl. C.C. & S. Judge, Bengaluru City (CCH-8).

Passed over The Counsel for Decree-holder is present submitted that as per the judgment in WP No.29299/2013 dated 23-10-2024 in case of Mahindra and Mahendra Finance Service Limited v/s K V Chandrashekar and others, the payment of court fee does not arise in respect of award for recovery of money. On perusal of above said judgment. In para 20 observed that award granting recovery of loans advanced does not qualify as an instrument chargeable under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act. In para 21 it observed as follow: An arbitral award should not be subject to any stamp duty under the broad provisions of Section 3(b) when read with Sections 19(a) and (b) due to its unique intangible nature and legislative oversight, which distinguishes an award from other instruments enumerated in the schedule of the Act, which, if executed outside the State of Karnataka and then enforced in the State, would typically incur the stamp duty. And held that stamp duty cannot be subjected to award. The above said judgment is applicable to the case on hand, the facts are similar to that case. Accordingly, office objection is over ruled. Business Text: Case has been called out. Decree holder is present. Counsel for decree holder filed memo. The counsel for Judgment debtor filed objections to I.A. No.1. Case will be taken at post lunch. Case is taken at post lunch. Decree holder and his counsel present. The Judgment debtor and counsel absent. The counsel for the Decree holder addressed the arguments on I.A. No.1. As there is no representation on behalf of Judgment debtor, therefore arguments on I.A. No.1 is taken as not canvassed. Having heard the arguments through the counsel for the Decree holder, I have perused the records. The I.A. No.1 is find U/sec. 151 of Civil Procedure Code on 16.12.2024 by the Decree holder requesting to appoint court Commissioner to break open the lock of the premises to get the physical possession of schedule property. The Judgment debtor in his objections has contended that he has handed over the keys of the premises on 20.01.2024 to the Decree holder. But to substantiate the said fact nothing has been produced. Therefore, it appears that the Judgment debtor still has not deliver the possession of the schedule property. It is evident from the records that the Decree has been passed in favour of the Decree holder directing the Judgment debtor to deliver the vacant physical possession along with arrears of rent and damages along with interest. There is nothing on record to believe that the said Judgment has been either challenged or reversed. Hence, it is just and necessary to appoint the court commissioner to execute the Decree. So, to meet the ends of justice, I proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A. No.1 dated 16.12.2024 filed the Decree holder U/sec 151 of Civil Procedure Code is allowed. Hence, court commissioner Mr. Prakash Hande who is an Advocate has been appointed to carry out commissioner work. The Decree holder is permitted to pay commissioner fee of Rs.5,000/- to the commissioner directly. The court commissioner is directed to deliver the physical possession of the suit schedule property to the Decree holder after breaking open the lock of the premises. Further it is made clear that the concerned jurisdictional police Rajarajeshwari nagar, shall co-operate to the court commissioner in executing the commissioner work. In view of the above, commissioner warrant is issued and also necessary intimation to the jurisdictional police. For report of the commissioner. Call on 24.01.2025.

Business Text: Application filed by the DHR is hereby allowed. Office to transfer the decree to the court of Principal Civil Judge & J.M.F.C. Maddur.
Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 03/08/2024]
Order Procedural History: ORDERS Learned counsel for DHR has filed application U/Sec.151 of CPC r/w Rule 106(4) of Karnataka Civil Rule of Practice stating that the JDR is the resident of Maddur Taluk, Mandya District and movable and immovable properties are situated at Maddur Taluk, Mandya District. Hence, prays to hand over the decree transfer petition to the decree holder's hands for being presented and executed through the Principal Civil Judge & J.M.F.C, Maddur, in the interest of justice and equity. Heard the learned counsel for DHR and perused the materials placed before me. On going through the execution petition it seems that the JDR is the resident of Maddur Taluk, Mandya District and also perused the award passed by this Court, which shows that the JDR is directed to pay a sum of Rs.2,99,000/-. As per order XXI Rule 5 of CPC – “Where a decree is to be sent for execution to another Court, the Court which passed such decree shall send the decree directly to such other Court whether or not such other Court is situated in the same State, but the Court to which the decree is sent for execution shall, if it has no jurisdiction to execute the decree, send it to the Court having such jurisdiction”. In the circumstances, I pass the following: ORDER Application filed by the DHR is hereby allowed. Office to transfer the decree to the court of Principal Civil Judge & J.M.F.C, Maddur. In support of his application DHR has sworn to an affidavit wherein it is stated that Judgment Debtor is residing outside the territorial jurisdiction of this court and transmitting the decree transfer petition through court from this court to jurisdictional court of Maddur will take considerable time and even he may not able to know about exact date of transmission of such orders. Therefore prayed to transfer the decree to the Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Maddur by handing over the decree transfer petition to the hands of the decree holder. The decree holder has assigned a reason that Judgment Debtor is residing outside the jurisdiction of this court and it is stated that he is residing in the jurisdiction of Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Maddur. Hence there is no impediment to transfer the decree to the Principal Civil Judge & JMFC, Maddur. The DHR has sought to handover the decree transfer petition to him for presentation before Principal Civil Judge & JMFC, Maddur. Since the DHR himself has sought for handing over the decree it is just and proper to handover the decree to the DHR for presentation before proper court. Hence the following: ORDER The application filed by the DHR under section 151 CPC r/w Rule 106(4) of Karnataka Civil Rules of Practice is hereby allowed. The decree is ordered to be transferred to the Principal Civil Judge & JMFC, Maddur. A copy of the order transferring the decree together with the accompaniments mentioned in Rule 6 of Order XXI of the Code to be taken to the court to which they are to be sent are ordered to be handed over to the counsel for decree holder on obtaining due acknowledgment.

It is seen from the records that the DHR has filed an application seeking attachment and sale of schedule property belong to the JDR for realization of the decree amount. However, the JDR has failed to discharge the decree liability. Hence, the DHR is entitle to proceed against the attached property for recovery of the decree amount. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:- Ex.No.1177/2024 O R D E R Accordingly, the office is hereby directed to draw up the sale proclamation in respect of attached schedule property of JDR in accordance with the provisions of order 21 Rule 66 of CPC. Business Text: The present petition arises out of the decree passed on a compromise petition filed by the parties in O.S.No.370/2021 on 22.04.2022. 2. The parties had agreed that the amount of Rs.4,20,000/- shall be waived off from Rs.16,20,000/- that was due. The amount payable would be Rs.12,00,000/-. Thereafter, the defendant/ lessee shall pay Rs.45,000/- continuously without any enhancement as monthly rent to the owner/ lessor. The amount of rent had fallen due since May, 2022. 3. The compromise petition was accompanied by a schedule for payment of the amount that fell due. The decree holder and the judgment debtor have filed the memo of calculation independently. According to the decree holder, the actual amount received from the judgment debtor is Rs.15,15,000/-. Whereas according to the judgment debtor payment made by him until now is Rs.16,00,000/-. The amount that is said to have been paid for which documents are placed on record by the judgment debtor is Rs.7,04,900/- and Rs.1,00,000/- payment made to Smt.Shwetha Maruthi. It is not clear as to who this Smt.Shwetha is which is not specified by the judgment debtor. The judgment debtor is found due in Rs.11,25,000/- towards arrears of rent till the filing of the petition. Even assuming the payment of Rs.15,15,000/-, the judgment debtor would be due in a sum of Rs.23,25,000/-. The judgment debtor would be due in a sum of Rs.8,10,000/-. 4. Now, the learned counsel for the judgment debtor asserts that, in respect of the amount due towards arrears of rent, the decree holder is required to file a separate claim. This apparently is an absurd submission considering the basis on which the compromise petition came to be filed. The decree holder had waived off Rs.4,20,000/- from the amount due and now the judgment debtor submits that, the decree holder has to come up with a fresh petition to recover the amount due under the compromise petition. 5. Considering the conduct of the judgment debtor, I am not inclined to hold that, the decree holder has to file a fresh petition. The judgment debtor in fact has to pay the amount due to the decree holder in order to claim full satisfaction. Office is therefore directed to issue arrest notice to the judgment debtor for payment of the amount due of Rs.13,50,000/-. Call on 21.07.2025.
